The interbars sample

Barred galaxies caught before, during and after an encounter with a neighbour. Every plate is 70 kpc across, so sizes compare directly between galaxies. Open a plate for its record and the raw spectrum of its nucleus. In lecture 2 you choose one system and measure its emission lines.

Things to look for
  • The bar: a straight, bright structure through the centre.
  • Signs of the encounter: tails, bridges, a disturbed or double nucleus.
  • In the spectrum: are Hα and [O III] strong emission lines, or is the nucleus mostly starlight (Ca H+K, Mg b, Na D)?

No system matches that search.

Images: Legacy Surveys DR10. Spectra: SDSS DR17 (3″ fibres) and DESI DR1 (1.5″ fibres), the main galaxy’s nucleus, DESI where both exist, normalised at 5500 Å. Stage from a visual classification of the images. Distances for H₀ = 70 km/s/Mpc.
